extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Congress, federal policymakers, and designers of national science policy/administrative agencies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative standards for creating a postwar national research agency (the proposed National Research Foundation), including its purposes, organization, authorities, patent policy, and procedures for release and publication of wartime scientific results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security restrictions: prompt release
rubrics_metrics.description: Except to the extent that military security dictates otherwise, wartime scientific information and experience should be spread upon the record for the benefit of the general public; material still subject to security classification should be released as soon as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Release classified material when there is ground for belief that the enemy cannot turn it against us. Much information needed by industry and education can be released without disclosing military embodiments. Broad dissemination furnishes a sounder foundation for national security than continued restriction which would impede our own progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination of declassification and release
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans for release must recognize that research was carried out under many auspices (Army, Navy, OSRD, NACA, departments, educational and industrial organizations) and should be coordinated so one agency's release does not unfairly conflict with restrictions elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate release with allies for jointly possessed classified information to minimize international friction. Uncoordinated release harms morale and scientific cross-fertilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board to control release
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a Board, made up equally of scientists and military men, to pass upon declassification and control the release for publication of scientific information which is now classified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency recommending release should be an Army, Navy, civilian body, well grounded in science and technology, competent to advise the Secretaries of War and Navy, and of sufficient recognition to secure prompt, practical decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement and facilitation of publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies (governmental and private) possessing scientific information released from security control should adopt measures to encourage and facilitate preparation and publication of reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Get scientific material to scientists everywhere promptly and at as low a price as consistent with suitable format; prepare manuscripts while staffs still assembled and records accessible; facilitate dissemination to men studying overseas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal government new responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Government should accept new responsibilities for promoting creation of new scientific knowledge and developing scientific talent in youth, and make Federal funds available to discharge these responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should minimize driving out funds from local governments, foundations, and private donors, but some displacement risk must be accepted given national need for better scientific research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focal point agency for non-governmental basic research
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be a focal point within the Government — an over-all agency — devoted to supporting basic research conducted outside Government, coordinating research programs of national importance, formulating national policy toward science, sponsoring interchange of scientific information, and ensuring incentives in industry and universities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such an agency is necessary to furnish funds to colleges/universities, coordinate where possible, and serve as the effective discharge point of the new responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve departmental research groups' roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Groups within Government departments (Agriculture, Commerce, Interior, Federal Security Agency) whose interests are primarily those of scientific research should remain where they are and continue present functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These groups' largest contribution lies in applying fundamental knowledge to departmental problems; they should not be made the repository of new, large national research responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent agency for basic research (no operating agency placement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A new, independent agency should be established to support basic research and advanced scientific education alone; it should not be an adjunct or subdivision of an operating agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operating agencies have immediate operating goals and production pressures unfavorable to basic, speculative research. Basic research is inhibited by conventional approaches and cannot be satisfactorily conducted where gauged by production standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency should not operate laboratories; use contracts/grants
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency should promote research through contracts or grants to organizations outside the Federal Government and should not operate any laboratories of its own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support of basic research must leave internal control of policy, personnel, and methods to the institutions receiving funds; the agency should be independent yet responsible to President and Congress under usual fiscal controls adjusted for research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fund stability and multi-year commitments (Five Fundamentals #1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever the extent of support, there must be stability of funds over a period of years so that long-range programs may be undertaken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods should permit commitments of funds from current appropriations for programs of five years duration or longer. Continuity and stability expected from Congressional appreciation and ongoing quality that yields continuing support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency membership selection on merit (Five Fundamentals #2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency administering such funds should be composed of citizens selected only on the basis of their interest in and capacity to promote the work of the agency, persons of broad interest and understanding of scientific research and education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members should not be otherwise connected with Government or representative of any special interest (see later detailed Member appointment provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote research via contracts/grants and not run labs (Five Fundamentals #3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency should promote research through contracts or grants to organizations outside the Federal Government; it should not operate any laboratories of its own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinforces independence and supports dissemination of funds to institutions best suited for basic research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave internal control to recipient institutions (Five Fundamentals #4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support of basic research in colleges, universities, and research institutes must leave internal control of policy, personnel, and the method and scope of the research to the institutions themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protection of institutional autonomy is of the utmost importance to preserving research quality and freedom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency accountability to President and Congress (Five Fundamentals #5)
rubrics_metrics.description: While assuring independence and freedom for research, the Foundation must be responsible to the President and the Congress; usual controls of audits, reports, budgeting, etc., should apply, adjusted as necessary for research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only through such responsibility can the proper relationship between science and democratic governance be maintained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civilian-initiated, civilian-controlled military research
rubrics_metrics.description: Military preparedness requires a permanent, independent, civilian-controlled organization with close liaison to the Army and Navy, funded by Congress, with the clear power to initiate military research supplementing Service-conducted work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-range research on military problems should be civilian-conducted by universities and industry scientists; Services should continue research to improve existing weapons; placing civilian military research within the proposed agency would balance military and other research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purposes of the National Research Foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation should develop and promote a national policy for scientific research and education; support basic research in nonprofit organizations; develop scientific talent by scholarships/fellowships; and by contract support long-range military research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These overarching purposes guide the Foundation's Divisions and programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and selection of Members (Foundation Members)
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsibility should be placed in, say, nine Members not otherwise connected with Government nor representative of special interests, selected by the President on the basis of interest and capacity to promote Foundation purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested terms of 4 years with no immediate reappointment after a full term; staggered initial appointments so at least two Members appointed each year; Members to serve without compensation but receive expenses; Members elect their chairman annually; director appointed by Members; director salary adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative staffing and civil service appointments
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be an administrative office responsible to the director handling fiscal, legal, personnel, and related administrative functions; except for director, division members, and one executive officer per division, all employees should be appointed under Civil Service regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures professional administration while allowing key leadership flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization: professional Divisions and initial list
rubrics_metrics.description: The Members should establish several professional Divisions responsible to them. At the outset Divisions should include: (a) Division of Medical Research; (b) Division of Natural Sciences; (c) Division of National Defense; (d) Division of Scientific Personnel and Education; (e) Division of Publications and Scientific Collaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each Division has a specific function (support medical research; support physical and natural sciences; support long-range scientific research on military matters; support scholarships and fellowships; encourage publication and international exchange).

rubrics_metrics.name: Division membership appointment and nominations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Division should be made up of at least five members appointed by the Members of the Foundation; the Members should request and consider recommendations from the National Academy of Sciences which should establish a nominating committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chairman of each Division appointed by the Members. Division members' terms determined by Members; they may be reappointed; receive expenses and per diem compensation (example: $50/day) with an annual cap (example: $10,000).

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of National Defense specific representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Membership of the Division of National Defense should include, in addition to five civilian members, one representative designated by the Secretary of War and one by the Secretary of the Navy, serving without additional compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures military liaison and representation within the Division while maintaining civilian-led structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Members' powers and duties (functions a–o)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Members of the Foundation should have powers to: (a) formulate overall policies; (b) establish and maintain offices as necessary; (c) meet/function anywhere in U.S. territories; (d) obtain/utilize services of other Government agencies; (e) adopt/promulgate/amend/rescind rules and regulations; (f) review and balance financial requirements and propose annual estimates with appropriations earmarked by Division purposes; (g) make contracts or grants for research by negotiation without advertising for bids; (h) create advisory/cooperating agencies and councils and pay expenses thereof; (i) enter into contracts/grants with educational and nonprofit research institutions; (j) initiate/finance research related to national defense; (k) initiate/finance projects for which existing facilities are unavailable or inadequate; (l) establish scholarships and fellowships; (m) promote dissemination of scientific and technical information and international exchange; (n) support international cooperation in science via financial aid for meetings, societies, and international programs; (o) devise and promote methods improving transition between research and practical application in industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many functions should be exercised with advice of relevant Divisions; appropriations should be earmarked for Division purposes but Foundation has discretion over expenditures; freedom to place contracts by negotiation is critical to secure creative research capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisions' responsibilities (program, allocation, review, liaison)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Division is responsible to the Members for: (a) formulation of programs and policy within its scope; (b) recommendation regarding allocation of research programs among organizations; (c) recommendation of arrangements between Foundation and organizations selected; (d) recommendation of arrangements with State and local authorities regarding scholarships/fellowships; (e) periodic review of the quality of research under the Division and revision of support program; (f) presentation of budgets; (g) maintaining liaison with other scientific research agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisions thus carry substantive programmatic and evaluative duties, including quality review and budget presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent policy principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation should protect the public interest while leaving cooperating organizations adequate freedom and incentive: the Government should normally receive a royalty-free license for governmental purposes under any patents resulting from Foundation-financed work; there should be no obligation to patent discoveries; no absolute requirement that rights be assigned to Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether assignment of rights is required should be left to discretion of the director and interested Division in special cases; legislation should leave patent policy discretion to Members so arrangements may be adjusted as circumstances require.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for private employment of Members/division members (special authority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislation should specifically authorize Members and Division Members to engage in private and gainful employment, notwithstanding restrictive provisions against dual interests, provided no compensation is received from any profit-making institution which receives funds under contract or otherwise from the Division concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relaxation of prohibitions is justified to secure part-time services of highly competent men who otherwise could not serve; safeguards prevent conflicts of interest with funded institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom from usual bidding/procurement rules for research contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Because research differs from standard procurement, the Foundation should be freed from the obligation to place research contracts through advertising for bids and should be free to place contracts/grants with demonstrated research institutions and with other promising institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Success of research contracts is measured qualitatively; the Foundation must be able to contract by negotiation to secure creative talent and latent research promise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research contract fiscal flexibilities and waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation should be authorized to make, modify, or amend contracts of all kinds with or without legal consideration and without performance bonds; to allow advance payments at Director's discretion; and to relax the General Accounting Office's normal vouchering requirements for research contractors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colleges and universities are not equipped to handle detailed vouchering/auditing technicalities required of commercial contractors; strict adherence to normal fiscal procedures would impair research efficiency and increase Government cost unnecessarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research contracts on actual cost basis without profit
rubrics_metrics.description: Research sponsored by the Foundation should, in general, be conducted on an actual cost basis without profit to the institution receiving the research contract or grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows wartime precedent (OSRD) where research was conducted on cost basis; measure of successful contract is contribution to knowledge, not price.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program growth and budgetary timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The program should grow from modest beginnings to a stable level over several years; estimates for first and fifth years of operation should be prepared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuity and stability of funding are essential; early Congressional action is imperative and legislation must be drafted carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative action and urgency
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislation creating the Foundation is necessary, should be drafted with great care, and early action is imperative to meet the challenge of science and utilize its potentialities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization described is an outline; detailed suggestions in appended committee reports should aid drafting; whatever program is established must satisfy the Five Fundamentals.
